Among 200k+ list-price trades in memory.jsonl since 15:00, 28 talks ended 14 deals and 14 no-deals. 8 of those 14 no-deals were three pairs retried across orders, all with a budget at or below the list price: 25620027 with G1d19ebee (curtain, list 229000) 4 times, with budgets 225540, 223750, 194340 and 185260, i.e. limits of at most 206100; 25620027 with G1465c678 (carpet, list 307000) twice; and dae-yangkim with G1465c678 twice. The same pairs failed again at 15:27, 15:29, 15:32 and 16:40, and the carpet at 15:40, 15:41, 15:44 and 15:44. Each retry uses up one of the 3 tries and the 300 s kit window, which could go to a pair that closes. Across the whole trace, the 200k+ list-price band had 109 talks, 39 deals and 70 no-deals, so the lost deals are the lever. The change is not the tuning team's 'route away from pairs that repeatedly drop' idea. That idea is covered by the existing 900 s scout-drop and quick-reject avoid list, and this change is the missing case: a negotiated no-deal.

spec.why: Counts from traces/memory.jsonl: 349 of 1,423 buyer trades are no_deal with an empty asks list, and 252 of those are TASK_STATE_REJECTED with no price. The same pair repeats across hours. SKU Gc01583a5 at shop 25512088 has 5 quick rejects at different budgets and food_hours (540, 540, 360, 180, 72), and it was rejected again at 22:48. The 900 s avoid in `main` (buyer_r3.py:424) expires between orders, so these dead pairs keep coming back as candidates. Each one then wastes a slot against the 300 s kit limit and the RETRY_UNTIL cut-off that ends further tries. A one-hour avoid for proven dead pairs frees those slots for live shops, which should raise buyer_close_rate and deals. I did not count the repeat rate across every pair, so this is not as well backed as it could be.
